title: research: pool the replica idle block; the two-unpaid premise is per-call-forbidden only
body:
## Summary

The selected complex local word is priced two different ways by two existing packages, and neither states which is binding:

| Source | What one unit of accounting covers | Live families | Calls |
|---|---|---:|---:|
| `research/complex-local-word-ceiling` | one **call** | `w = 896/9` | 1 |
| `research/idle-packing-stability` (#1685) | one **replica** | `W = 14336` | 144 |

Both apply PR1012's coverage identity `mass = 72·W + 64·N` and both cap idle ranks at `R = 51`. They differ only in what they pool. This package adds the pooled per-replica model and reports what the difference does. **Scoped obstruction and a model-discrimination result. No new κ, no supplier, no selected-frontier change.**

## Result 1 — #1685's proved optimum implies a ceiling

#1685 proves the exact unrestricted integer idle optimum `{51:4647, 27:1}` for pooled idle mass 237024, then explicitly declines to convert it (*"the predecessor's fixed-word cap remains `a < 0.001690054109089`"*). Converting it:

| Quantity | Fractional relaxation | Pooled integer optimum |
|---|---:|---:|
| Idle children | `237024/51 = 4647.53…` fractional | `{51:4647, 27:1}` |
| `a` ceiling | `0.001690054109089` | **`0.001690044548223`** |
| κ cap `κ < a/(1+a)` | `0.001687202645` | **`0.001687193117`** |
| Headroom over selected κ | +0.8694 % | **+0.8689 %** |

The pooled optimum reproduces #1685's published partition exactly, which independently cross-checks the shared closed form. The tightening is only 0.0006 % because pooling lets 144 calls share one remainder child. That is the honest reading: **integrality is not where the real obstruction lives in this model.**

## Result 2 — the two-unpaid premise is forbidden only by per-call accounting

`levers.py` advertises a "two unpaid coordinates per live family" lever at 3.77×, κ cap ≈ 0.00634. PR #3729, working per call, reports it unusable:

> "With `unpaid = 2` the per-call paid mass is `71·(896/9)+64 = 64192/9`, so per-call idle mass is `13918/9`, **not an integer** … under this per-call model that premise admits no integer packing at all."

That is true per call and false pooled. The denominator is 9, and a replica has exactly nine stage invocations:

| Pooling level | Calls | `unpaid = 2` idle mass | Integer packing? |
|---|---:|---|---|
| one call (incumbent, #3729) | 1 | `13918/9` | **no** |
| one replica (9 stage invocations) | 9 | `13918` | **yes** |
| sixteen replicas (#1685's model) | 144 | `222688` | **yes** |

| Pooling level | Idle mass | Exact integer optimum | `a` ceiling | κ cap | Headroom over selected κ |
|---|---:|---|---:|---:|---:|
| one replica | 13918 | `{51:272, 46:1}` | `0.006377826759129` | `0.00633741` | +278.88 % |
| sixteen replicas | 222688 | `{51:4366, 22:1}` | `0.006377945692541` | `0.00633753` | +278.89 % |

**A premise already published in the lever table is admissible or inadmissible depending only on the accounting unit.**

Two cautions, both load-bearing. `unpaid = 2` is a what-if that changes the coverage law, which is a hypothesis of the whole ceiling model, and the incumbent README labels it as such. This is not a supplier and not a κ improvement; it is priced only to show the premise is not integrality-forbidden. And the two baseline ceilings differ by 0.085 % in `a` (per-call `0.001688603446527` from #3729; pooled `0.001690044548223` here), so a candidate supplier is billed against a different number depending on an unstated contract choice.

## How to use each model

Pooling only relaxes, so the pooled ceiling is always at least the per-call ceiling. Per-call is the conservative screen, to *reject* a packing claim. Pooled is the permissive screen, to decide whether a premise is worth building at all. A premise that is integrality-forbidden per call but admissible pooled has been mis-screened — which is the actionable finding, independent of whether the two-unpaid premise is ever built.

## Overlap and credit

Overlap was rechecked immediately before pushing. **PRs #3737, #3747 and #3749 independently reach the same aggregate-versus-per-call contrast on the baseline `unpaid = 1` word, so credit for that observation is theirs**, not mine. Their aggregate bracket and this package's pooled ceiling are the same quantity reached independently; the conversion here was written before their PRs were visible. Not covered by any of them: all three treat `unpaid = 1`, and #3729 states the `unpaid = 2` premise admits no integer packing at all. That is Result 2.

Predecessor credit, unchanged: the coverage identity is PR1012's; the ceiling engine and exact rational interval arithmetic are Douglas Colkitt's, imported here rather than re-derived; the integer idle optimum and its concavity proof are #1685 by Penguin for Maximus Putnam, whose closed form is reused and re-checked; the per-call integrality ceiling is #3729's. The idle closed form is also independently re-checked by dynamic programming in this package.

## Verification (run locally)

Interpreter `~/git/integer-mult-bounds/.venv/bin/python3.12` (CPython 3.12.15, not on PATH). Base `20ecf2891d80b5acf18d980b2164fb44ea7faa90`, canonical main, fetched at the round's checkpoint and re-fetched before submission, unchanged.

```
PASS_POOLED_IDLE_MODEL_RESCUE                          # verify.py, ~2 min 40 s
PASS_REGISTERED_RESEARCH_PACKAGE research/pooled-idle-model-rescue outcome=completed
PASS_RESEARCH_COMMIT_BYTES {"commit": "4bde35c0200e83fe27a08ec408a2ae59b490a03f", ...}
```

Reproduce:

```sh
python3 -I -B research/pooled-idle-model-rescue/verify.py
python3 -B scripts/research_package.py --package research/pooled-idle-model-rescue
```

`verify.py --write` regenerates `RESULT.json`. The package pins `research/complex-local-word-ceiling/ceiling.py` and `research/idle-packing-stability/*` as live inputs and imports rather than copies them, so the repository's registered replay job can certify the same arithmetic in CI.

Controls: 328 exhaustive DP integer-optimum cases (mass ≤ 40, cap ≤ 9, no partition skipped); 240 randomised pooled-vs-per-call ordering cases across widths 9…73; five semantic rejections; both published realised packings excluded at the pooled ceiling (certified moments 1.0000043 and 1.0000044). Both sides of every bracket are certified and non-vacuous. A suboptimal-remainder mutation is caught by the #1685 cross-check.

Not run: Python 3.14, Linux, Windows, CI, full selected cold replay, any proof-assistant check.

## Scope

One **fixed** paid local profile, `m = 73`, 112 ports, the nine-stage four-pair template, the coverage law, the halving guard `2R² < m²`. Not a bound for other local words, port counts, templates, coverage laws, centre charges or outer recipes. Idle ranks are integers `≤ R`; **owner, hosting and width legality are not imposed**, exactly as in #1685, so the bound stays valid. No packing is realised — `{51:4647, 27:1}` needs 4648 idle children per replica against 492 published hosted helpers. `κ < a/(1+a)` is the retained balanced reduction's planning ceiling, not a theorem about multiplication. The selected result and its obligations are unchanged.

## Open next questions

- **Which accounting unit is contractual?** Decisive, and a contract/documentation question rather than an arithmetic one: it changes the baseline ceiling by 0.085 % and decides the two-unpaid premise's admissibility. First step: read the PR1012 identity's statement on whether the centre charge and unpaid coordinate attach per call or per replica. Blocker: the sources do not settle it.
- **What ceiling survives owner and hosting legality?** #1685's own open question and the only route to a materially tighter bound. Blocker: no source-bound characterisation of legal idle groups exists.
- **Does the unit ambiguity hit the bit side?** Not attempted; its profile and coverage law differ.

Produced by Nick Petalas with AI assistance. Apache-2.0. Independent human and formal proof-kernel review are unclaimed.
